nodes.text: Let me paint a picture for you. It is 8:30 am. I am in my car, hair wet from a shower just waking up. No food or liquid in me still a bit dreamy and dazed from a restful night's sleep. It's too early for me to determine how this day may fare. I turn the heat up, the radio on and I set out for the daily grind.

A squirrel is standing in the middle of the road, her bushy tail rigid, flicking back and forth like a rattle. She's just standing there, chattering away. My car is stopped maybe twelve or so feet in front of her. It's a quiet mid-town suburban road, damp with wet and soggy leaves. And the squirrel stands defiant.
She shall not let me pass. I inch forward six inches or so. The squirrel chatters and pounds her tail left and right, to and fro, in agitation.

To emphasize for effect, I'm having a Mexican stand-off with a squirrel. I say it's a she because despite the serious cojones shown, I see no obvious squirrel package up front. In human reckoning, no hairy beach ball gonads.
In my experience, these agile beasts invite death upon themselves with regular abandon. I am confused and a little awed by my cute and fuzzy nemesis.
I inch forward six inches or so. The squirrel chatters and pounds her tail left and right, to and fro, in agitation.
Wet leaves stick to the windshield wipers.

Since I don't speak squirrel or chipmunk or whatever form of rodent language they chirp away in, I can't query the beast to find out why it refuses me passage. I admire the cunning creature and its show of fortitude so I back up, turn around and go down the street the other way.

In my rearview mirror, the squirrel contemplates its victory on the battleground known as Michigan Street and basks in the glory of the moment. It will tell the tale of staring down a one ton vehicle, an eighth ton human, and coming away victorious.
These are a few truths I came away from and they are thus:

1. I lack the necessary skills to adequately confront a squirrel poised in the middle of the road refusing to budge.
2. (or) I am a sucker for being punctual and on-time.
3. (most assuredly) The tree rodent uprising is at hand.
Addendum, from my notes on the matter:

They have the position and means to attack our network of communication and utility. They have the numbers to swarm us en masse. They are a reckless, stupid and suicidal species. They eat their young for breakfast, stuffing their cheeks on babyflesh.
They know where we live, they know our routine, they watch from above, stashing their stores for the armageddon they will unleash upon us all.
